transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-01-22
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 58 minutes
Recording: yes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Ethan Ross (Redwood SE), Aisha Khan (Coral Head of ML), Ben Turner (Coral Platform Eng), Luis Gomez (Coral SRE)

Summary (auto):
Quick scoping for a 3-week POC to validate latency SLOs across Coral's 7B / 30B model mixes. Focus: TTFT vs TPOT, p95/p99 targets, sampling strategy, synthetic vs production replay, and measurement instrumentation. Decided on next steps: share harness, provide token distribution, schedule two benchmark windows.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya: alright everyone, thanks for joining, uh quick roll call, i'm maya from redwood, ethan is with me on the se side. can you hear us ok?
[00:06] Aisha: yep, loud and clear. aisha here.
[00:08] Ben: ben on the platform team, hi.
[00:10] Luis: luis, sres.
[00:12] Ethan: awesome. goal for today is to lock the poc success criteria and the measurement plan, so when we run benchs we have clear pass/fail.
[00:20] Aisha: great, high level we run conversational summarization in prod, normally 1k token prompts with 200-400 token responses. throughput needs to be ok for interactive UI — we care a lot about first token.
[00:30] Maya: noted. can you confirm model footprints? are you primarily on a 7b family or mixing 30b?
[00:36] Aisha: mix. baseline traffic is 70% 7b, 30% 30b. open to quantized variants for cost savings but we need to see latency viability.
[00:44] Ethan: helpful. for clarity, we'll be measuring TTFT (time-to-first-token) and TPOT — total per-request token time — and reporting p50/p95/p99. any target guesses from your slos?
[00:56] Ben: we currently aim for p95 TTFT under 300ms for 7b in our UI. p99 is fuzzy, we'd accept higher but want to measure. for 30b aiming p95 < 600ms if feasible.
[01:10] Maya: ok, that's a good starting point. proposal for the poc acceptance: two axes — latency SLO and functional correctness (no regressions in output quality). SLO criteria: p95 TTFT <= 300ms (7b), p95 TTFT <= 600ms (30b); p99 TTFT <= 900ms (both) as soft guardrails. For TPOT we suggest p95 <= X ms per token — we'll convert to tokens/sec expectations; e.g., p95 TPOT for median 1k-token runs should keep total response time < 2s on 7b in batch-optimized mode.
[01:38] Aisha: when you say TPOT per token, is that measured including pre-processing and network hop? we need to isolate runtime.
[01:46] Ethan: good call — measurement plan will separate client-side and infra-side. instrumentation will capture: ingress latency, queuing, scheduler batching delay, model runtime (token emit), egress. TTFT measured at model emit time (server-side) and also we record first-byte at client to capture network.
[02:02] Luis: i want KV cache warm vs cold included. our typical flows are many short-step chats where cache matters. we need runs for cold start and warm cache steady state.
[02:10] Maya: agreed. Poc will include two phases: warm-cached steady-state (30 minutes sustained traffic) and cold-start ramp tests (full restart + 100 request burst).
[02:20] Ben: what about batching? we run in multi-tenant pool, so batching will vary. can we simulate both optimized single-tenant reserved capacity and shared hosted (noisy) environment?
[02:30] Ethan: yes, we'll run profiles: dedicated-like (pinned capacity, low batching jitter) and shared-like (variable batching). we'll include tail simulation with background noise traffic to emulate noisy neighbors.
[02:40] Aisha: sampling — how many requests do you need for p95/p99 to be statistically meaningful?
[02:44] Ethan: good question. recommended: for p99 stable estimate aim for ~100k samples per profile. p95 converges faster — 10k–20k samples. but we can do tiered approach: small pilot to sanity check then full sweep.
[02:56] Maya: to keep the poc short (3 weeks), plan: week 1 gather artifacts and small pilot; week 2 full sweeps on 7b and 30b; week 3 analyze and remediation (config tuning, quantization).
[03:09] Aisha: sounds reasonable. on security — we need SOC2 evidence, KMS integration, and assurance around logging. do you capture audit logs and can they be routed to our SIEM?
[03:20] Maya: yes, Redwood can provide SOC2 attestation and audit log delivery options. for Private we support customer KMS; for hosted we can integrate with customer-managed KMS in the VPC option. i'll send the certs and docs.
[03:30] Luis: network wise we'll want ephemeral peering for the test window. ben will coordinate.
[03:34] Ben: yep. i'll propose 3 candidate windows next tuesday/thursday.
[03:38] Ethan: instrumentation detail — we'll tag spans with request_id, model_variant, quantization flag, sequence_length, batch_size, and cache_hit boolean. we'll compute TTFT as time from model_dispatch to first_token_emit and TPOT as model_runtime / tokens_emitted aggregated at request level.
[03:56] Aisha: let's try to define pass/fail bullets so success is unambiguous.
[04:00] Maya: proposed success criteria: 1) p95 TTFT <= target (300ms for 7b, 600ms for 30b) during warm steady-state under target load (TBD RPS), 2) p99 TTFT <= 900ms for steady-state, 3) no more than 1% of requests return runtime errors or OOMs, 4) output quality measured by automated eval set shows <3% regression vs your baseline.
[04:24] Aisha: that quality metric is key. we'll provide an eval set. do you support round-trip evaluation scripts?
[04:30] Ethan: yes we'll run eval harness comparing rouge/bertscore and our manual spot checks. will report delta.
[04:36] Ben: load shaping — our UI load profile is spiky; peak 200 concurrent, avg 40. we'll provide RPS histogram.
[04:44] Maya: we'll convert that to synthetic load curves: ramp to peak over 5 min, hold 10 min, step down, repeat. include sudden 10x burst test.
[04:54] Luis: what about measuring tail from batching interactions — sometimes a 99.9 spike happens because of a large seq length in batch. can we stratify by seq_len buckets?
[05:01] Ethan: yes. we'll produce bucketed p95/p99 by seq_len (0-256, 257-512, 513-1024). also by cache_hit true/false, and by quantization flag.
[05:12] Maya: agreed. responsibilities recap — redwood provides harness, runs, and analysis; coral provides traffic histograms, private peering, and eval set.
[05:21] Aisha: timeline ok for us. couple of items — we may need a dedicated capacity trial if shared hosting fails to meet p95. will that be part of the poc scope?
[05:30] Maya: we can include a short dedicated capacity test if the shared run fails certain thresholds. that will help isolate noisy neighbor effects. we'll treat it as an optional branch and pre-configure capacity estimates.
[05:40] Ben: pricing / cost estimate for the poc?
[05:42] Maya: we'll send an estimate in the follow-up email — approximate GPU hours for full sweeps and optional dedicated window.
[05:48] Aisha: final question — can we get token-level billing traces to map cost per inference?
[05:52] Ethan: yes, the console provides token-level cost and latency breakdowns per-route. we'll export per-request token counts and cost attribution.
[05:58] Maya: ok wrapping up. i'll email the harness, security docs, and proposed run slots. any other open Qs?
[06:03] Aisha: none from me, thanks.
[06:05] Ben: all good.
[06:06] Luis: good, thanks.
[06:08] Maya: thanks everyone, we'll follow up. bye.

References mentioned:
- Benchmark harness (to be shared): contains load config, synthetic generator, and trace collector.
- Eval set: Coral will supply labeled prompts/responses.
- Security pack: SOC2 attestation + KMS integration note.

Notes on measurement specifics (post-call):
- Statistical plan: p95 reported with 95% CIs, p99 with bootstrapped CIs due to tail variability. Aim for >10k samples for p95, >50k for p99 when possible.
- Sampling windows: 30-minute steady-state windows repeated 3x, plus 10 restart cold-starts.
- Metrics exported: TTFT_server_ms, TTFT_client_ms, TPOT_request_ms, tokens_emitted, batch_size, cache_hit, model_variant, quant_flag, seq_len_bucket.
- Acceptance gating: automatic — if p95 TTFT exceeds target by more than 10% in two consecutive steady windows for same profile, remediation triggers (tuning, quant relax, or dedicated run).

End of transcript.
